r6-methodology-fair.title: Measurement fairness
r6-methodology-fair.imperative: Read bitrepro_spike.py + the reused #356 helpers. Confirm identical seeds/data/config across conditions, only the determinism/seeding knob varies, no knob also changes the data, drift = max-abs state_dict diff, wall-time honest (warmup discarded, threads pinned in all conditions). Flag any methodology flaw. Record pass/fail.
r6-methodology-fair.finding: Measurement is FAIR. (1) Identical seeds/data/config: every condition builds the SAME jobs via production build_main_train_backtest_jobs (modules, train_years=[2022,2023], eval_year=2024, max_rounds=1, epochs=2, seed=0 from _write_config); spike never passes seed_override, so no condition trains a different seed. (2) Only the knob varies: per condition the sole difference is the torch determinism flag (use_det / warn_only) and optional preseed=torch.manual_seed(0); none of these alter jobs/data/config. (3) In-process verified: run_jobs(n_workers=1) -> _run_in_process runs worker_fn(job) directly in the spike process, so flags/preseed ARE in effect during training. (4) Baseline genuinely single-threaded: _run_in_process calls init_worker(threads=1) every run, so set_num_threads(1) applies in ALL conditions incl baseline -- threads are NOT the varying knob. (5) Drift = max-abs state_dict diff across both modules (_max_weight_diff). (6) Wall-time honest: discarded warmup absorbs cold-start; per-run perf_counter; ratios vs baseline mean. No knob changes the data; no condition compares different seeds. No methodology flaw found.

r7-reproduce-numbers.title: Numbers reproduce
r7-reproduce-numbers.imperative: Re-run the harness independently. Confirm baseline drift ~3.6e-4 order-of-magnitude (>> 1e-6) and seeded conditions EXACTLY 0.0, strict mode does not raise and emits zero nondet warnings, cost ~1x. Record observed values. Record pass/fail.
r7-reproduce-numbers.finding: REPRODUCED independently (my re-run, torch 2.10.0+cpu, exit 0). Observed drift: baseline=3.712e-04, deterministic-strict=3.027e-04, deterministic-warn=3.358e-04 -- all ~3e-4 order-of-magnitude, ~300x above the 1e-6 bar. baseline-seeded=0.000e+00 and deterministic-strict-seeded=0.000e+00 -- EXACTLY 0.0, matching the load-bearing claim. Strict mode did NOT raise (status ok, raised=null) and emitted ZERO nondeterministic-op warnings in both strict conditions. Cost ~1x (x_baseline 0.99-1.10, all noise; flags add nothing meaningful). Numbers differ from the report at the 4th sig-fig as expected (run-to-run FP), but the ORDER OF MAGNITUDE and the seeded-==-0.0 result reproduce decisively.

r8-rootcause-in-code.title: Root cause verified in code
r8-rootcause-in-code.imperative: Read training.py (fork_rng/manual_seed block) + network.py (Dropout). Confirm training-loop dropout draws from unseeded process-global RNG because fork_rng restores global state on exit, and the loop runs in train mode (no eval()). Confirm random.Random(seed) governs only shuffling. Record pass/fail.
r8-rootcause-in-code.finding: ROOT CAUSE verified in code. training.py:95-97 seeds torch ONLY inside 'with torch.random.fork_rng(): torch.manual_seed(seed); module = module_cls(config)' -- fork_rng() restores prior global RNG state on exit, so only module INIT is seeded. The training loop (lines 131-156) calls module.predict_pairwise(batch) in the module's DEFAULT train mode -- grep confirms NO .train()/.eval() before the loop (the only .eval()/.train(was_training) pair is lines 379/429 inside _evaluate_module's try/finally, used during validation only). network.py:37 defines nn.Dropout(p=config.dropout) reused 3x in the backbone (config dropout=0.2), the ONLY stochastic train-mode op in the package per grep (no torch.rand/bernoulli/multinomial elsewhere). So train-mode dropout samples from the UNSEEDED process-global torch RNG, which varies run-to-run. random.Random(seed) (line 98) is a SEPARATE Python RNG governing only batch shuffle, not dropout. Diagnosis holds: it is a seeding-placement bug, not kernel/intrinsic FP nondeterminism. The manual_seed->0.0 experiment is the matching empirical proof.

r10-gonogo-sound.title: GO/NO-GO soundness
r10-gonogo-sound.imperative: Judge whether NO-GO on the literal det-flags criterion (3.6e-4 >> 1e-6) and GO-signal via a one-line training.py seeding fix (0.0 at ~1x) follow soundly from the numbers, with honest caveats (bounded scale; multi-thread BLAS could reintroduce FP drift). Record pass/fail.
r10-gonogo-sound.finding: GO/NO-GO sound. NO-GO on literal criterion is correct: 'deterministic mode' = set-flags call reaching drift<1e-6 at<2x; measured strict drift ~3.6e-4 is ~360x over the 1e-6 bar, so it fails the drift bar despite meeting cost (1.03x). Flags-buy-nothing is well-supported: zero nondet warnings + flag flip moves drift only within FP noise => the governed ops are not the cause (F2/F3). GO-signal via a training.py global-RNG seeding fix is justified: seeded conditions hit EXACTLY 0.0 at ~1x, and that fix is a production change correctly deferred to G4. Caveats are honest and non-overclaimed (0.0 only at bounded #356 scale; multi-thread BLAS reduction-order FP could reappear, where use_deterministic_algorithms -- shown free + non-raising -- becomes the right guard). Note for Commander (not a blocker): the diagnostic preseeds the GLOBAL RNG before the whole run, so the precise placement of manual_seed in G4 (govern the loop without re-perturbing module init) is a design choice G4 owns; the spike says 'move/duplicate' and does not overclaim one exact line. Recommendation follows soundly from the numbers.
